title: Ortho Para Meta Directors Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A new student sits by a friend, a magnet pulls a pin to its ends, and chimney smoke leaves black soot. Seats are not random, and some soot hides a danger. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) we learn directive influence of groups on the benzene ring, and carcinogenicity.

On the molecule bench, curved arrows push the lone pair of OH into the ring and make ortho and para rich, while nitro pulls electrons out and sends the new group to meta. Then the groups sorted link by link (activating ortho para directors, deactivating meta directors, and halogens as the odd ones), the nitration of toluene and nitrobenzene, and why polynuclear hydrocarbons from incomplete burning are carcinogenic. Then the exam trap, an original JEE/NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 97 of our PUC Chemistry series, and the last of Class 11.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:

0:34 Ortho, meta and para
1:03 The molecule bench: phenol, a giver
1:39 Nitrobenzene, a puller
2:00 Pause and think: CH3 or CHO
2:16 Sorting the groups, link by link
2:59 Worked example: nitrating toluene and nitrobenzene
3:33 Carcinogenic polynuclear hydrocarbons
4:00 Exam trap: halogens
4:20 Practice question (JEE/NEET pattern)
